messages:
Maya: Quick check — new microanchor-256 embeddings on the holdout set show weird cluster sparsity: lots of tiny clusters and one huge hub. recall@10 dropped from 0.84 -> 0.72 after INT8 per-channel quantization. Anyone else seeing hubbing?
Jorge: Yep saw something like that with microanchor-v2 on short queries. Do you have silhouette and cluster-size distribution?
Maya: Quick stats pasted: recall@1 0.52, recall@10 0.72, mean_cluster_size 12.3, median 3, max 174, silhouette -0.06. Indexing: Faiss HNSW, efSearch=64, efConstruction=200.
Priya: Can you share the quant pipeline config? per-channel vs per-tensor? symmetric/asymmetric?
Maya: ```
quant: int8
mode: per_channel
scheme: asymmetric
calibration: minmax
```
Jorge: Per-channel int8 has bitten us on long-tail anchors before. Try per-tensor symmetric as a quick compare. Also ensure L2-normalize before indexing.
Maya: Ran per-tensor symmetric quick run: recall@10 0.78, recall@1 0.56, silhouette -0.01. Better but still some hubbing.
Sam: What pooling / layer are we using for embeddings? CLS vs pooling matters here.
Maya: pooling: mean, layer: last_hidden.
Carla: Could be tokenization mismatch too; but first try topk normalization (divide by sqrt(sum squares)) and re-check cluster balance.
Maya: Reran with L2 normalize + per-tensor int8: recall@10 0.80, silhouette 0.02. Promising — reduced hubs — but a tiny precision hit on some short queries (~0.01 recall@1).
Priya: Can you paste a couple of qualitative failure cases where per-channel failed but per-tensor succeeded?
Maya: ```
Query: "best budget headphones"
GT: [doc23, doc78, doc104]
per-channel top1: doc999 (wrong)
per-tensor top1: doc23 (correct)
---
Query: "reset router dns"
GT: [doc11, doc45]
per-channel top1: doc47 (wrong)
per-tensor top1: doc11 (correct)
```
Jorge: Let's also compute recall@k broken down by cluster percentiles — hubs vs tail. If hubs dominate nearest neighbors, per-channel quant might be amplifying certain directions. I'll prep a per-cluster breakdown.
infra-bot: Job 18273 queued on eval-queue-fast (estimated 18m).
Maya: Filed ENG-ML-813 with dataset links and configs. Next steps: sweep per-tensor vs per-channel (int8 symmetric/asymmetric), with/without L2, measure recall@1/5/10, silhouette, cluster-size-90pct, and per-cluster recall. Priya -> run sweep, Jorge -> per-cluster breakdown, Sam -> collect qualitative failures.
Sam: :thumbsup:
